stdout.pattern:
usage: git2 [--help] [-c <key=value>] [--config-env=<key=value>] [--no-pager]
             [--version] <command> [<args>...]

These are the git2 commands available:

   add          Add file contents to the index
   blame        Show the origin of each line of a file
   branch       List, create, or delete branches
   cat-file     Display an object in the repository
   cherry-pick  Apply the changes introduced by an existing commit
   checkout     Switches branches or restores working tree files
   clone        Clone a repository into a new directory
   commit       Record changes to the repository
   config       View or set configuration values 
   demo         Demonstrate libgit2 functionality
   describe     Give an object a human readable name based on an available ref
   diff         Show changes between commits, trees, etc
   fetch        Download objects and refs from another repository
   for-each-ref  Output information on each ref
   hash-object  Hash a raw object and product its object ID
   help         Display help information
   index-pack   Create an index for a packfile
   init         Create a new git repository
   log          Show commit logs
   ls-files     Show information about files in the index
   ls-remote    List references in a remote repository
   merge        Join development histories together
   note         Manage notes attached to objects
   push         Update remote refs along with associated objects
   rebase       Reapply commits on top of another base tip
   remote       Manage remotes
   reset        Reset HEAD, index, or working tree
   rev-list     List commits in reverse chronological order
   rev-parse    Parse revision specifications
   show-index   Display the contents of the index
   stash        Stash changes in a dirty working directory
   status       Show the working tree status
   submodule    Manage submodules
   tag          Create, list, or delete tags
   version      Show application version information
   worktree     Manage multiple working trees

See 'git2 help <command>' for more information on a specific command.
